quiz.title: Module 1 — The Principles of Good Design
quiz.description: Monday's quiz covers the principles of good design — balance, unity, contrast, leading lines, repetition and pattern, rhythm, proportion and variety — and how each one is applied in a composition.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of balance in graphic design?
options: To make every element in a design the same size
To create stability by distributing visual weight throughout a composition
To ensure that every element uses the same colour
To make the design as colourful as possible
questions.explanation: Balance is about visual weight, not sameness. Distributing that weight across the composition is what gives a design stability.

questions.prompt: A designer uses a consistent colour palette and illustrations that share the same visual style throughout a flyer. Which principle of design does this demonstrate?
questions.explanation: A consistent palette and a shared illustration style make separate elements read as one piece. That sense of everything belonging together is unity.

questions.prompt: A magazine cover uses a large, bold headline and smaller supporting text to help readers identify what they should read first. Which principle is being applied?
questions.explanation: The size and weight difference between the headline and the supporting text is contrast, and here it is doing the work of telling the reader where to start.

questions.prompt: A designer uses several lines that point towards the main image on a poster, directing the viewer's attention to it. What is this technique called?
questions.explanation: Lines that guide the eye towards a focal point are leading lines — a deliberate way of directing attention rather than hoping the viewer finds it.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between repetition and pattern in graphic design?
options: Repetition is used only in branding, while pattern is used only in posters.
Repetition creates contrast, while pattern creates balance.
Repetition involves repeating a single element, while pattern involves repeating multiple design elements.
Repetition creates movement, while pattern eliminates movement.
questions.explanation: Repetition is one element used again; pattern is several elements repeated in a recurring arrangement. Both create consistency, but at different levels of complexity.

questions.prompt: A designer repeats triangular shapes in different sizes and colours to give a concert flyer an energetic, flowing appearance. Which principle is primarily responsible for this organised visual tempo?
questions.explanation: Repeated shapes that carry the eye through a composition at a particular pace create rhythm — the visual equivalent of a beat.

questions.prompt: A poster features a large title, a medium-sized quotation, and smaller body text. Why is this arrangement an example of good proportion?
options: It makes all the information equally important.
It ensures that the design contains only three text elements.
It creates a relationship between elements by using sizes that reflect their relative importance.
It eliminates the need for contrast.
questions.explanation: Proportion is the relationship between sizes. Scaling text to match how important it is tells the viewer what matters most without them having to read a word.

questions.prompt: A designer combines geometric shapes, organic imagery, and different typefaces in a composition while ensuring the elements still work together. Which principle encourages this kind of interesting variation?
questions.explanation: Variety is what keeps a composition interesting — different shapes, imagery and typefaces give the eye something to move between, provided they still hold together.
